- WireGuard peer configs and NAT traversal details
- KV cache persistence and S3-compatible endpoint for model artifacts
- Runbook acceptance: rollback criteria, canary traffic %, escalation matrix
- Evidence needed from Acme for audit (SOC2 baseline items we discussed)

Can the Acme infra team confirm a 2-hour cutover window on Thu 7/8 between 01:00-03:00 UTC? If that works, Kimberly and I will attach the final reference diagram and ops checklist for your engineering lead to sign off.

Attachments (drafts to follow in separate message): vpc-reference-diagram-v2.pdf, ops-handoff-checklist.xlsx

- Acme infra lead: Sam Evans (assumed)

Thanks,

Jordan,

Thanks — confirming the team saw this. A few quick clarifications before we commit to the window: 

1) Firewall rules: we need the exact control-plane IPs or FQDNs for your control plane (including healthcheck ranges). Can you confirm a static /29 or provide a short-lived IP set?
2) WireGuard: our security team prefers manual key rotation on first boot; can you provide the peer config template and expected MTU?
3) Artifact storage: we can host an S3-compatible endpoint in our colo but need the expected object sizes and lifecycle rules (retain for 30/90 days?).

Cutover window: Thu 2026-07-08 01:00-03:00 UTC is tentatively ok for us. Procurement copied for notification; they may request a formal maintenance notice 7 days prior.

Subject: Re: On-prem VPC onboarding & ops handoff — cutover readiness

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick read. A few concrete answers and I've attached the reference files to this message. See attachments: vpc-reference-diagram-v2.pdf, ops-handoff-checklist.xlsx, wireguard-peer-config.txt

Quick answers inline: 

1) Control plane endpoints: we will publish three static IPv4s (control-plane cluster) and one IPv6 where available. I put the exact /32s in the diagram legend (see page 1). If you need them in CIDR /29 for firewall groups we can provide the aggregated set; confirm which you prefer.

2) WireGuard peer config: attached template includes a key-rotation note. MTU recommended 1420 (default) but we can adjust for your edge NAT. Our templates assume the peer key is rotated once post-provision; ops checklist includes validation commands.

3) Artifacts: typical model bundle objects are 50-600MB; we recommend lifecycle rules to keep latest 14 days and archive older than 90 days. If Acme needs longer retention for audit, we can adapt S3 lifecycle and provide a retention-proof snapshot step in the runbook.

Runbook / rollback summary (short): 
- Canary routing: 10% traffic to Redwood runtime variant A for 30 minutes, monitor latency and error rate.
- Automatic fallback: if 5xx > 1% or 95th p90 latency > 2.5x baseline for 5m, revert route to previous model variant and scale down new nodes.
- Manual abort path: if healthchecks fail during initial scaling, ops run rollback playbook and preserve logs/artifacts for postmortem.

Requested signoffs: 
- Sam (Acme infra): confirm firewall CIDR choice and acceptance of MTU/rotation approach
- Procurement: confirm maintenance notification cadence
- Marissa/Sean (Redwood): approve escalation contacts (Marissa primary, Sean secondary)

I'll also upload a locked PDF of the diagram to the Drive link and send DocuSign for the maintenance agreement after Sam confirms.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Lead Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Once Sam confirms the IP approach, I'll trigger DocuSign for the ops agreement and we'll begin the pre-cutover checklist on Wed (dry run). Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth cutover.
